results.label: this tree ships the M111 calendar-read state vocabulary (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the module still requires nothing at all: no app module, no database, no fetcher, no helper
it still reads no environment, no filesystem and no path, so it cannot be configured from outside itself
it still calls no clock of its own and takes its instants as arguments
a copied module makes the same decisions as the shipped one, including the new state mapping
exactly the three shipped files that already reached it still do — M111 added no importer, so the state cannot leak into a module that had no reason to know it
and M111 added the vocabulary to the SAME file as the two clocks, so the module count did not grow
no shipped file mentions a probe, the shim or the test support, so the fix is in the app and not in its harness
the market layer is NOT rewired to the harness: it still reads the real feed URLs, and its own failure path is what M111 classifies
the API documentation names the three states and the fact that unknown is not a pass, so the contract is written down where a client reads it

scope: M111 portability: the vocabulary is a leaf, and nothing shipped mentions the harness: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
